newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ITC sees strong growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: India's ITC sees strong growth ahead.

text.p: Indian tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC Ltd said on Saturday that investments in technology and products by the company would ensure strong returns in future.
"The first two months of the company's operations during the current financial year have registered impressive results, auguring well for the future," the company said in a statement.
ITC Ltd is 31.7 percent owned by Britain's B.A.T. Industries plc.
ITC Ltd posted a net profit of 3.47 billion rupees ($ 97 million) in 1996/97 (April-March) compared with 2.61 billion rupees in the previous year.
The company's board recommended a dividend of 40 percent in 1996/97 compared to 25 percent in the previous year.
ITC's gross income increased to 59.60 billion rupees, or 15 percent, and the profit before tax rose increased by 30 percent to 5.87 billion rupees in 1996/97, it said.
The company plans to invest 19.0 billion rupees in the next five years to position itself as the market leader in the sectors in which it operates, the statement said.
It also plans to invest in hotel properties through greenfield projects and acquisitions directly, as well as through its subsidiary ITC Hotels Ltd, it added.
The company has launched two new brands of cigarettes to consolidate its position as country's leading cigarette manufacturer, it said.
ITC's leaf tobacco exports increased by 30 percent in volumes and 65 percent in value in 1996/97.
